newsitem.title: USA: Mossimo sees earnings below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Mossimo sees earnings below estimates.

text.p: Mossimo Inc said Wednesday that earnings for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year would fall below analysts' estimates although sales would be up about 50 percent from a year earlier.
Earnings for the fourth quarter should be $0.03-$0.08 a share, Mossimo said, compared with estimates of about $0.18. In the 1995 quarter it earned $0.19 a share.
Sales should be near $27 million for the quarter and more than $100 million for the year, it said.
Earnings for the year will range between $0.72 and $0.77 a share, down from $0.89 last year, it said.
It said the earnings shortfall was caused by an inventory shortage and late product deliveries in the holiday season, which forced the company to make price concessions to retailers.
Anthony Cherbak, chief financial officer, said in a statement that Mossimo had "modified its 1997 plan" to expect sales growth of about 15 percent for the year.
Operating margins should be roughly 12-14 percent in the first half of 1997 and grow moderately through the year, he said.

Cherbok said rapid 1996 growth strained Mossimo, delaying shipments and causing lower operating margins because of high levels of out-of-season merchandise. He also cited "unusually high product development costs" in the third quarter.

"We continue to take aggressive corrective measures to address these operational issues, including filling several key management positions over the last five months, and expect to realize the benefits of these enhancements in the second half of 1997," said Cherbak.
